routes.description: Establish that neither deterministic causation nor indeterministic chance supplies the ultimate authorship implicated in libertarian free will, while separating useful accountability practices from ultimate blame.
routes.successCriteria: Show that first-person authorship and exact-condition alternatives are unsupported, that fuller causal knowledge undermines ultimate desert, and that social regulation remains available on pragmatic grounds.

motionBridge.description: Determinism and indeterminism must both fail to provide ultimate authorship or a genuinely open alternative under identical conditions.

centralBridges.description: The freedom at issue must include the first-person authorship and alternative possibilities that compatibilist competence does not supply.
Unchosen neural states, inherited traits, environments, and prior causes must explain conduct without making the conscious person its ultimate origin.
Ultimate blame must be distinguished from contracts, deterrence, restraint, treatment, and other forward-looking responsibility practices.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Advance neural prediction must illuminate how conscious awareness follows rather than ultimately originates unfolding thought and action.
Sensitivity to small, unchosen causal variations must remain relevant even when practical capacities and character differences are acknowledged.

routes.description: Establish that freedom worth preserving consists in reasons-responsive, temporally extended self-control and socially formed competence rather than metaphysical independence from causation.
routes.successCriteria: Show that capable agents retain meaningful control and alternatives, that impairment remains distinguishable from ordinary causation, and that responsibility practices sustain reasonable social expectations.

motionBridge.description: Reasons-responsive agency and morally relevant freedom must remain possible whether underlying physical processes are deterministic or indeterministic.

centralBridges.description: A naturalistic account must preserve the responsibility-relevant content of free will after magical or libertarian commitments are removed.
Control must consist in competent responses to reasons across practical possibilities rather than authorship of every causal input or neural detail.
Ordinary responsibility must rest on capacities, reasonable expectations, excuses, and enforceable rules without requiring absolute self-creation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Alternative possibilities must be grounded in an agent's real range of competences and nearby causal variations rather than atom-for-atom replay.
Authorship must operate through planning, training, and temporally extended control without conscious selection of every microscopic step.

sections.title: The concept and burden of free will
sections.rationale: The motion turns first on whether naturalistic reasons-responsive competence preserves the freedom at issue or instead omits indispensable first-person authorship and alternative possibilities.

sections.title: Alternative possibilities and causal luck
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether nearby counterfactual variation supports a meaningful ability to do otherwise or instead exposes consequential action as dependent on unchosen physical differences.

sections.title: Capacity, causation, and ultimate blame
sections.rationale: The competing accounts must explain whether normal competence remains responsibility-grounding despite universal causal wiring and whether unchosen formative conditions defeat ultimate blame.

sections.title: Pragmatic responsibility and social enforcement
sections.rationale: The debate must distinguish metaphysical desert from the forward-looking roles of legal boundaries, deterrence, treatment, contracts, expectations, and public protection.

sections.title: Prediction and conscious authorship
sections.rationale: Advance prediction and unconscious generation test whether authorship requires conscious microscopic origination or can instead consist in planned, practiced, temporally extended control.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Compatibilism risks changing the subject because purifying a concept can discard features indispensable to what people mean by free will.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: The enduring free-will problem concerns first-person authorship and the ability to do otherwise, neither of which is supplied by determinism or indeterminism.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: When minute neural differences determine major life choices, the universe rather than a conscious self controls the outcome in a way that challenges ordinary personhood.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c02.proposition: Although undetermined choices would not be free, tiny unchosen neural differences can still determine consequential actions and radically alter a life.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c03.proposition: Complete causal understanding would make ordinary wrongdoing resemble an exculpatory brain-tumor case because the agent did not author the decisive neural conditions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c05.proposition: Capacities differ, but genes, upbringing, environment, and persuasive inputs are unchosen, making ultimate blame unjustified while leaving pragmatic accountability useful.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c09.proposition: Tracing a lapse to earlier conduct uncovers further unchosen causes, while contracts, confinement, accountability, and public safety can be preserved without ultimate self-authorship.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-03.proposition: If severe antisocial behavior became causally understood and reliably curable, treatment would replace retributive punishment and reveal apparent evil as a condition rather than self-authored wickedness.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-07.proposition: If a person's words could be recorded before conscious awareness, that foreknowledge would undermine free will because consciousness enters too late to originate the unfolding action.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-09.proposition: Compatibilism preserves third-person competence but forfeits the first-person freedom people value because the agent could not act otherwise under identical conditions.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Compatibilism can preserve a naturalistic meaning of free will by refining inherited concepts instead of treating their magical interpretations as definitive.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Free will is the reasons-responsive competence to control an agent's practical degrees of freedom, and that capacity rather than indeterminism grounds responsibility.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: An agent can meaningfully have been able to do otherwise when a small variation would produce another choice, even if the decision process is deterministic.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Small variations can flip balanced decisions, while strongly reason-dominated decisions require larger changes, so causal sensitivity does not by itself defeat freedom.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c04.proposition: Being causally wired is not equivalent to being impaired, so exceptional neurological disability cannot justify treating every normally capable agent as exculpated.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c06.proposition: Control consists in responding competently to factors one did not choose, and moral education enables people to become and remain practically responsible self-controlling agents.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-02.proposition: Rejecting absolute responsibility does not eliminate ordinary responsibility, whose point is a consequentialist system of reasonable expectations, excuses, and enforceable social rules.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-04.proposition: Even with diagnosable and curable antisocial dispositions, credible punishment would remain necessary because anticipated sanctions and shared enforcement sustain lawful cooperation.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-06.proposition: Current neural decoding is not real-time foreknowledge, and prediction interacting with its subject faces self-referential limits, so existing findings do not establish the proposed authorship-destroying scenario.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-08.proposition: Authorship does not require conscious control of every microscopic step; agents author actions through practiced capacities, advance planning, and temporally extended macro-level control.
